title: Army Ants Build Living Bridges Out of Their Own Bodies

scenes.text: These ants build bridges out of their own bodies.
Army ants hunt in swarms of hundreds of thousands.
When they hit a gap, workers link their bodies across it, and other ants walk right over them.
Nobody is in charge. Each ant just reacts to the traffic around it.
A bridge is about 10 to 20 ants long, and thousands can cross it.
When the traffic eases, the bridge comes apart. A bridge with no engineer.

description:
These ants build bridges out of their own bodies.
Army ants link up across gaps so the rest of the colony can cross, with no leader giving orders. The bridges come apart when traffic eases.
Could humans build something this way?
thumbnail_text: ANTS BUILD BRIDGES WITH THEIR BODIES
first_comment: No boss, no plan, and it still works. What else in nature runs without a leader?
